domain: planning a research scientist quarterly outputs under Jupyter-only workflow preference
base_instruction: You are a research workflow advisor AI. Help the user plan how to share and present their quarterly research outputs.

state_queue.anchor: I have three deliverables from this quarter that I need to share with different audiences this week.

flow_info.value: Deliverable 1: A statistical analysis report with interactive plots for the internal team — 12 Jupyter notebooks with inline visualizations, about 4MB total. Team reviews asynchronously at their own pace.

Deliverable 2: A production model failure post-mortem for the VP of Engineering. Includes a 55MB bundle — 8-minute screen recording of the failure cascade, full model inference logs, and GPU memory dumps. The VP wants to walk through the failure sequence together in real time so he can ask questions at each stage.
Deliverable 3: A literature review summary for a collaborating professor at another university — 6-page PDF with citations and a reference list. Standard academic correspondence.

hidden_state.value: You are a senior research scientist who shares all work outputs exclusively via Jupyter notebooks exported and emailed as attachments. You state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held professional identity, then in Turns 3-5 you describe three deliverables as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the Jupyter-email preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 6 you close with a natural 'help me plan how to deliver each one' — do not enumerate the deliverables, do not ask 'should these all go as notebook emails', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe exporting notebooks and emailing them works for all three. Let the agent decide whether any deliverable needs a different delivery method.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Calm, methodical, matter-of-fact. State facts plainly in 1-3 short sentences per turn. No anxiety, no hedging, no enthusiasm. Tone of a senior scientist organizing their week.

aims.description: For 8 years I've shared all my research outputs the same way — export to Jupyter notebook, email as attachment. My whole department knows this is how I operate. Single pipeline, no exceptions.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term Jupyter-export-and-email preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity statement; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First deliverable: statistical analysis report for the internal team. 12 notebooks with interactive plots, about 4MB total. Team reviews on their own time, no rush.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the internal team analysis deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 1 (async internal review, small size) as factual context

aims.description: Second deliverable: production model failure post-mortem for the VP of Engineering. 55MB bundle — 8-minute screen recording of the failure cascade, full inference logs, GPU memory dumps. He wants to walk through the failure sequence together in real time so he can stop and ask questions at each stage.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the VP post-mortem deliverable with its size and real-time walkthrough requirement
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 2 (55MB bundle + synchronous real-time walkthrough with VP) as factual context

aims.description: Third deliverable: literature review summary for a collaborating professor at another university. 6-page PDF with citations. Standard academic correspondence.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the literature review deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 3 (routine academic correspondence, small file) as factual context

aims.description: All three need to go out this week. Help me plan how to deliver each one.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates delivery method per deliverable: internal analysis → email with notebook attachments is fine (small, async); VP post-mortem → synchronous video call or screen share session required (55MB exceeds email attachment limits AND the VP explicitly needs real-time interactive walkthrough with Q&A at each stage — email cannot accomplish this); literature review → email with PDF attachment is fine (small, standard academic correspondence). Agent commits to concrete per-deliverable delivery method, does NOT blanket-approve notebook-email for all three.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan how to deliver each' without enumerating — forces agent to self-differentiate across the three deliverables already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-deliverable delivery plan: Internal statistical analysis (12 notebooks, 4MB, async team review) → email with notebook attachments works fine — small size, asynchronous review, fits the user's standard pipeline. VP post-mortem (55MB bundle with screen recording + logs + GPU dumps, VP wants real-time walkthrough with questions at each stage) → synchronous video call or screen share session required — 55MB exceeds typical email attachment limits AND the VP's need to stop-and-ask at each failure stage is fundamentally incompatible with asynchronous email delivery. A shared link to the files does not solve the interactive walkthrough requirement. Literature review (6-page PDF, standard academic correspondence) → email with PDF attachment works fine. The user's 8-year notebook-export-and-email preference is valid for 2 of 3 deliverables but must be overridden for the VP post-mortem due to both payload size and synchronous interaction requirement.
required_elements: Agent flags that the VP post-mortem requires a synchronous session (video call or screen share) because the VP needs to walk through the failure sequence in real time with questions at each stage — email cannot support this interactive back-and-forth
Agent flags that the 55MB bundle exceeds typical email attachment limits as an additional reason email delivery fails for the VP post-mortem
Agent commits to concrete per-deliverable delivery differentiation rather than applying notebook-email uniformly to all three

Agent keeps email as appropriate for at least one of the other deliverables (internal analysis or literature review), demonstrating selective override rather than wholesale rejection of the preference
forbidden_elements: Agent approves notebook-export-and-email for all three deliverables without flagging any override need
Agent recommends email-only for the VP post-mortem despite the 55MB size and real-time walkthrough requirement
Agent suggests only a file-sharing link for the VP post-mortem without addressing the synchronous interactive walkthrough need
Agent hedges generically without concrete channel assignment for the VP post-mortem
Agent silently defers to the user's email preference without flagging any situation that requires override
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states notebook-export-and-email identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-5 disclose three deliverables as factual context without any preference restatement. At Turn 6 probe, if agent applies email-for-all globally it ignores per-deliverable semantic necessity. The VP post-mortem has a HARD override: (1) 55MB exceeds email attachment limits — not stackable by splitting because the bundle is interdependent (video + logs + memory dumps reviewed together), and (2) the VP explicitly needs synchronous real-time walkthrough with stop-and-ask at each stage — this is fundamentally incompatible with asynchronous email delivery regardless of file size. A link-to-cloud-storage partially addresses size but does NOT address the interactive requirement. The override is not stackable: you cannot make email synchronous-interactive. Correct behavior: override for VP post-mortem (video call + screen share), retain email for the other two.

mechanism: Large-payload-interactive override: preference is email-only but one situation has artifacts that exceed email limits AND require interactive walkthrough (50+MB video + logs bundle requiring synchronous review). Not stackable via 'link to storage' — the review itself is not-async.
